candidates.title: Clinical features of long-term survivors treated with botensilimab plus balstilimab in refractory MSS metastatic colorectal cancer
candidates.evidence_status: SITC poster 472 is listed on sponsor publications page; primary poster text was not exposed. Sponsor release is a locator only. Prior full-cohort original journal abstract is available from PubMed and publisher search indexing.
candidates.prior_primary_cohort_findings: Previously treated MSS mCRC without active liver metastases, n=123; median follow-up 20.2 months. Safety/tolerability was primary; OS exploratory. ORR 21% (95% CI 14-29), median PFS 4.0 months, median OS 21.2 months (95% CI 16.2-23.8), 36-month OS 33% (95% CI 24-43). Common treatment-related AEs: diarrhea 39% (grade >=3, 8%) and fatigue 37% (grade >=3, 2%). These are earlier cohort results, not new Nov 9 data.
candidates.interpretation: The SITC analysis selects survivors of at least 18 months from the same cohort. Its conditional survival and response figures must not be presented as overall-cohort efficacy or as a randomized benefit estimate. No newer follow-up cutoff was verified.

papers.title: Long-Term Survival After CRS-HIPEC for colorectal Cancer Peritoneal Metastases
papers.access: Complete open-access publisher HTML and 15-page PDF inspected; PDF pages 4 and 5 visually verified.
papers.design: Retrospective consecutive two-center Amsterdam cohort; October 2016 through December 2023; no randomized or untreated comparator.
papers.population: Colorectal peritoneal metastases after CC-0 CRS-HIPEC; PCI <=20; only successfully completely resected patients analyzed.
papers.endpoint_definition_note: Exact OS/DFS/PRFS time origins, censoring rules and competing-risk handling were not explicitly defined in the inspected Methods; do not supply inferred definitions as reported facts.

followup.CT_schedule: Every six months for first two years, beginning six months after surgery; annually thereafter.

source_discrepancies_requiring_resolutio: Table 2 CD>=3 aggregate is 227, but grade 3a+3b+4+5=234. 227 equals grades 3a+3b+4 only. Deaths may have been excluded from an aggregate labeled inclusive; do not silently correct it.
Table 3 other-recurrence median OS 17.5 has printed CI 44.3-56.2, which does not contain its estimate.
Narrative left-vs-right HR 0.718 and rectal-vs-right HR 0.542 disagree with Table 4 (left reference; right 1.533; rectum 1.271).

Narrative says metachronous timing loses multivariable significance; Table 4 early-versus-late HR 1.669, CI 1.076-2.590, p=.022, with categorical omnibus p=.067. These are different hypothesis tests and cannot be collapsed to a single unqualified statement.
Approximately 30% is variously described as disease-free long-term, OS beyond five years and possible cure. No consistently defined timepoint/denominator/CI supports a cure-rate extraction.

Figure 1 caption says 450 complete cytoreductions, whereas its exclusion box includes two incomplete cytoreductions. Discussion mentions approximately 10% excluded at exploratory laparotomy without reconciling that population with the 450-to-440 flow.
papers.interpretation: Selection and confounding prevent causal attribution to HIPEC. Never compare this median directly with randomized controls as evidence of benefit. Accessible full text meets access criteria, but safety and subgroup inconsistencies prevent a clean structured evidence card until reconciled. The source inconsistencies are reporting issues, not proof of misconduct.

papers.design_from_abstract: Retrospective analysis of prospectively maintained single-center 2007-2024 cohort. The title does not make this a prospective comparative trial.
papers.population: Rectal cancer complete or near-complete clinical responders after nCRT, selected for watch-and-wait.
papers.exact_pending_reason: Need authorized full text and supplement to verify eligibility/stage distribution, nCRT regimen, surveillance and endpoint definitions, at-risk denominators/CI, exact salvage counts, treatment/salvage morbidity, deaths and attrition handling. papers.limitations_visible: No surgical control; 26.5% attrition; evolving management across 17 years.

papers.title: A phase II pilot evaluation of lurbinectedin in patients with advanced gastrointestinal malignancies with DNA repair mutations
papers.access: Complete PMC primary report including Tables 1-2 and linked one-page Supplementary Table S1 reviewed. Registry page itself was not extractable; registry identity verified in paper.
papers.design: Single-center prospective open-label single-arm phase II; planned Simon two-stage 12 then 7 evaluable patients; stopped after eight for lack of response/activity.
papers.population: Adults with ECOG 0-1, unresectable/metastatic GI malignancy, measurable progressive disease and known/suspected deleterious DDR mutation; all enrolled patients had 2-5 prior treatment lines.

intervention.G_CSF: Protocol amended to add primary prophylaxis after neutropenia; pegfilgrastim 6 mg/cycle or filgrastim 5 microgram/kg/day for five days.

endpoint_definitions.PFS: First infusion to objective progression, clinical progression or death.
endpoint_definitions.OS: First infusion to death; censoring at last known alive.
endpoint_definitions.assessment: Radiologic/clinical assessment every six weeks; imaging at least every three cycles.
endpoint_definitions.safety_window: CTCAE v5; EOT 30 +/-7 days after last infusion, new antitumor therapy, or death, whichever first.

safety.SAE_terms: Abdominal pain (four events/three patients), sepsis, pulmonary embolism, fever, confusion, left DVT, constipation, gastric ulcer, S. pneumoniae pneumonia.
safety.treatment_related_deaths: No related SAEs reported; six deaths occurred overall, not a treatment-related mortality estimate.

papers.limitations: Only one rectal patient; no separate CRC outcomes. Single arm, n=8, heavily pretreated, heterogeneous DDR alterations, early termination and 5/8 receiving just one dose. Neither efficacy nor safety should be generalized to CRC.
papers.timing_note: New PubMed indexing, not a new November trial result. Paper also states prior AACR abstract/poster presentation on 2026-04-20.
papers.exact_pending_reason: Complete primary report is accessible, but only one rectal patient among eight mixed-GI patients and no separate CRC endpoints. Do not add the pooled outcomes to CRC-specific evidence rows.
